title: Cleary Gottlieb announces strategic partnership with Legora
author: Legora

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source directly supports the cluster’s proposition: Cleary plans firmwide Legora deployment after a pilot while stressing that value depends on strategic integration around identified, high-value workflows rather than software availability alone. It also supports the distinction between adoption and demonstrated outcomes because it reports no pilot metrics and presents efficiency and client-service benefits as anticipated claims.
qs: Following a successful pilot program in 2024, this strategic partnership will see Legora’s suite of AI-driven services, including new product features, fully rolled out across the entire firm.

“This is not about simply rolling out AI across the firm, but about engaging with identified, high-value use cases that enhance our ability to serve clients across practices, teams, and regions.”  About Cleary Gottlieb  Cleary Gottlieb is a leading international law firm with offices in key financial and business centers worldwide.

kp.k: Cleary expands Legora firmwide after 2024 pilot
kp.d: The May 1, 2025 announcement says Cleary Gottlieb will fully deploy Legora’s AI services across the firm following a pilot in 2024. The document characterizes the pilot as successful but provides no performance measures, evaluation methodology, or quantified results.
qs: Following a successful pilot program in 2024, this strategic partnership will see Legora’s suite of AI-driven services, including new product features, fully rolled out across the entire firm.

kp.k: Cleary targets efficiency and differentiated client work
kp.d: Cleary Managing Partner Michael Gerstenzang presents the partnership as part of embedding AI strategically into firm workflows, with the stated objectives of increasing efficiency and delivering differentiated, high-quality work to clients. These are Cleary’s stated aims rather than documented outcomes.
qs: “Cleary is committed to embedding AI into our workflows in strategic and competitive ways,” said Cleary Managing Partner Michael Gerstenzang.
“Partnering with Legora allows us to unlock efficiencies across the firm and deliver differentiated, high-quality work for our clients.”

kp.k: Legora supports document review, drafting, and collaboration
kp.d: Legora describes its platform as supporting collaboration between lawyers and AI across review and drafting workflows, including large-scale document review and Microsoft Word mark-up. The source claims that lawyers can complete end-to-end tasks more quickly and accurately, but it supplies no comparative study or measured accuracy and time-saving evidence.
qs: Cleary Gottlieb announced today a strategic partnership with Legora, a legal AI platform designed to transform the ways in which legal teams collaborate, review, and draft documents.
The platform is designed to allow lawyers to complete end-to-end tasks more quickly and accurately, enhancing the efficiency of workflows.
Legora helps professionals review tens of thousands of documents, supports mark-up in Word, and is enabled with world-class data partnerships and enterprise-grade security and privacy.

kp.k: Legora reports international adoption across 250 clients
kp.d: As of the announcement, Legora reports use by more than 250 clients in over 20 countries. The document does not identify those clients, define what constitutes use, or provide independent verification of these adoption figures.
qs: It is currently utilized in over 20 countries by over 250 clients.

kp.k: Partnership supports Legora’s North American expansion
kp.d: Legora CEO Max Junestrand identifies the United States as the leading market for innovative legal technology and frames the Cleary partnership as part of expanding Legora’s North American presence. His claim that firms such as Cleary will lead innovation and client service is forward-looking vendor commentary, not an evidenced finding.
qs: “The U.S. is the most important market for innovative legal technology,” Junestrand said.

“Legora is excited to expand our footprint in North America and partner with the pioneering lawyers at Cleary. In this fast-moving market, it will be firms like Cleary who lead the way and innovate in their ability to deliver exceptional client service.”

kp.k: Cleary combines vendor technology with custom AI development
kp.d: The Legora rollout is one component of a broader firm strategy that also includes Cleary’s acquisition of generative-AI developer Springbok. The stated purpose of the acquisition is to accelerate internal innovation and produce custom AI systems for particular clients and practice groups.
qs: Legora’s collaborative AI platform is one part of Cleary’s multi-faceted approach to driving AI integration across the firm.
Cleary recently acquired Springbok, a generative AI product development company, to accelerate innovation at the firm and develop custom AI builds for clients and practice groups.

kp.k: Specialist groups integrate AI into legal-service delivery
kp.d: Cleary identifies several internal groups with distinct AI-related functions: DLT applies AI to litigation needs, ClearyX develops technology-enabled transactional solutions, and Practice Innovation incorporates AI into legal-service delivery. The announcement does not quantify their effects on staffing, leverage, pricing, or client outcomes.
qs: Cleary's differentiated innovation strategy also encompasses the award-winning e-Discovery and Litigation Technology (DLT) group, which develops and leverages AI tools to meet client litigation needs, ClearyX, which focuses on emerging technologies to create efficient, cost-effective transactional solutions for clients, and Practice Innovation which infuses AI technology to empower the firm's delivery of legal services.

kp.k: Cleary prioritizes identified high-value AI use cases
kp.d: Director of Practice Innovation Ilona Logvinova says Cleary’s approach is selective rather than indiscriminate: AI adoption is to focus on identified, high-value applications that improve client service across practices, teams, and regions. The document does not specify the use cases or the criteria used to identify their value.
qs: “Our firm is committed to embedding AI in a way that is both strategic and thoughtful,” said Cleary Director of Practice Innovation Ilona Logvinova.
“This is not about simply rolling out AI across the firm, but about engaging with identified, high-value use cases that enhance our ability to serve clients across practices, teams, and regions.”

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Legora presents AI as augmenting lawyers' collaboration, document review and drafting; Cleary's leadership expects firm-wide efficiencies and differentiated client service.
pts.d: The Legora newsroom announcement describes its platform as designed to make end-to-end legal tasks faster and more accurate, with capabilities including large-scale document review and Word mark-up. These are stated capabilities and intended benefits, not quantified findings. Cleary Managing Partner Michael Gerstenzang says the partnership will enable efficiencies and differentiated, high-quality client work. The framing is collaboration between lawyers and AI, rather than autonomous replacement of lawyers.

pts.k: Cleary presents targeted AI integration and custom development as ways to improve legal service delivery across practices, teams and regions.
pts.d: The announcement places Legora within a broader strategy: acquiring Springbok to accelerate innovation and build custom AI for clients and practice groups, using AI tools for litigation needs, and incorporating AI into service delivery through Practice Innovation. Director of Practice Innovation Ilona Logvinova identifies high-value use cases, rather than deployment alone, as the mechanism for improving service. ClearyX is also described as creating efficient, cost-effective transactional solutions through emerging technologies, although that passage does not attribute those benefits exclusively to AI.

pts.k: Legora CEO Max Junestrand predicts that innovative firms such as Cleary will lead in client service and identifies the United States as the most important legal-technology market.
pts.d: Junestrand links the partnership to Legora's North American expansion and predicts leadership by firms like Cleary in a fast-moving market. This is an executive's market assessment and forward-looking expectation, without a specified forecast horizon or comparative market evidence.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers a pilot described as successful, reported adoption figures, organizational initiatives and executive statements, but no measured productivity or accuracy results.
pts.d: Team Legora reports a successful 2024 pilot as the background to firm-wide deployment, without describing its methods, scope or results. Reported use in over 20 countries by over 250 clients indicates adoption, not measured service improvements. The acquisition and internal innovation groups provide examples of implementation activity. Claims about efficiency, accuracy, quality and market leadership otherwise rest on platform descriptions and statements by Cleary and Legora executives; no benchmarks, comparative data or quantified client outcomes are supplied.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The May 1, 2025 announcement follows a 2024 pilot and anticipates firm-wide rollout without a completion date; benefits are linked to strategic workflow integration and selected high-value uses.
pts.d: The platform's capabilities and adoption are presented as current at publication. Full deployment, including new features, is prospective. Springbok's acquisition is described only as recent. Logvinova qualifies the approach as strategic and thoughtful, emphasizing identified use cases rather than rollout alone. Neither the expected efficiency gains nor Junestrand's prediction of market leadership has a specified achievement date.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The anticipated effects concern Cleary's lawyers and service teams, its clients, and Legora's position in the North American legal-technology market.
pts.d: Lawyers and legal professionals are expected to gain faster, more accurate workflows for review, drafting and collaboration. Cleary's practices, teams and regions are within the intended firm-wide scope, with litigation and transactional work specifically identified. Clients are expected to receive differentiated, high-quality services and custom AI builds. Legora, a legal-technology platform provider, expects to expand its North American footprint. The announcement does not claim staffing displacement, changes to professional roles or billing models, or wider access-to-justice effects.
